title: File the business tangible personal property (and machinery and tools) return
question: My business owns equipment. What do I file each year and when is the tax due?
office: Commissioner of the Revenue (assessment); City Treasurer (billing and collection)
summary: Every business in Charlottesville must report the equipment, furniture, computers and tools it owns, leases or uses on January 1 to the Commissioner of the Revenue. It is an itemized list with each item's original cost and year acquired. Manufacturers and some other businesses report machinery and tools instead. File in the online Business Tax Portal, or mail the city's return form. The form and the portal give a January 31 due date, but the city's tax page says March 15. Assessed value is 25% of cost in the first year, falling to 10%. The 2026 tax is $4.40 per $100 of assessed value. The Treasurer bills it in two halves, due June 5 and December 5, with no proration.

steps.step: Check whether your business must file
steps.who: Business owner (every business located in the city)
steps.how: If your business is located in Charlottesville and owns, leases, rents or borrows property it uses on January 1, you must report it. That includes furniture, fixtures, computers, phones, tools and machinery, items you have fully depreciated or expensed for federal tax, and personally owned items used in the business. The status and value of the property are fixed as of January 1. Check that the business address is inside city limits: the city's Business License Tax page says to look the address up on the city's GIS Viewer, because a business with a Charlottesville address may be in the Albemarle County portion, and Albemarle County runs its own process.
steps.deadline: Property owned or used on January 1 (the tax day)
steps.quote: All businesses located in the City of Charlottesville are required to file an itemized list of all property utilized in the business as of January 1st of each year.

steps.step: Work out whether you report business personal property or machinery and tools
steps.who: Business owner; the Commissioner of the Revenue sets the classification
steps.how: Manufacturers, mining operations, radio or television broadcasters, dairies, dry cleaners and laundries report their machinery and tools. They are not also taxed as business personal property on office equipment, furniture or fixtures. A business classified as a processor reports both. Every other business reports business tangible personal property. The same return form covers both: tick the box that applies.
steps.quote: Businesses subject to the machinery and tools tax are not subject to tangible personal property tax on office equipment, furniture or fixtures.

steps.step: New business: have the Commissioner set up your business tax account
steps.who: Commissioner of the Revenue, business tax office
steps.how: The online portal cannot open a new account or add a new tax type. New accounts are set up by the Commissioner's business tax office, in person, by phone or by email. For a new business this normally happens with the business license application, which is due within 30 days of starting the business and can be sent through the city's Secure Portal or mailed to P.O. Box 2964. The office then sends credentials for the Business Tax Portal. The Business License Tax page says a business license application also requires the business to file and pay business tangible property tax.
steps.quote: You cannot establish a business license account or create/register for a new business tax type through the portal.

steps.step: Prepare an itemized asset list and a list of leased equipment
steps.how: For each item, list the description, the date or year acquired and the original cost, plus the date of any disposal. Include freight, installation and sales tax in the cost. You can list items under $500 each, such as hand tools, as one total. Include operating-system software but not application software. Separately list property you lease, rent or borrow from others on January 1, giving the lessor's name and address, the property, the monthly rental cost and the lease dates. Leave daily rental property, vehicles licensed for the road, trailers, boats and aircraft off the leased list. Conditional sales leases count as purchases and go on the owned list. The form says the property must be substantiated by an asset or equipment journal, federal Form 4562 or Schedule L of Form 1120. You can use the city's Fixed Asset / Leased Equipment Schedule, or email an Excel listing to the business tax mailbox. A rendition such as Form 762 is not accepted in place of the schedule. State law also requires you to keep records good enough for the Commissioner to check the tax, and to open them for audit (§ 58.1-3983.1(K)).
steps.quote: Freight, installation and sales tax should be included in the cost of the property.

steps.step: File the return with the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.who: Business owner, filing with the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Filing for the year opens on January 1. If you have an account, file in the online Business Tax Portal. You need your mailing ZIP code, your six-digit account number and your SSN or EIN. Enter the cost of the prior year's acquisitions and disposals and upload the asset list, which the filing requires. Otherwise, complete and sign the paper Return of Business Tangible Personal Property or Machinery and Tools and mail it with the asset listing to Charlottesville Commissioner of the Revenue, P.O. Box 2964, Charlottesville, VA 22902. The Commissioner's page says business tax filings can also be left in the drop boxes on 6th Street and 7th Street or the drive-up box by the Key Rec Center. Do not send payment with the return. Signing certifies that the return is true: willfully signing a return you do not believe is true is a Class 1 misdemeanor (Va. Code § 58.1-11). Incomplete or unsigned returns are sent back and must be returned before the deadline.
steps.deadline: On or before January 31, according to the Business Tax Portal page and the return form. The Business Personal Property Tax page says March 15 (see caveats).
steps.quote: The return and list must be filed with the Commissioner of the Revenue on or before January 31 each year.

steps.step: If the business had no property in the city, still file and explain why
steps.how: File the return every year and explain how the business operates without assets, or name the entity that provides its property. A bare statement that you have no property is not accepted.
steps.deadline: Same due date as the return
steps.quote: If the business does not own or rent property, a return must be filed every year stating the reason that the business does not own or use any property.

steps.step: Manufacturers: report idle machinery and tools in writing by April 1
steps.who: Machinery and tools taxpayer, writing to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Idle machinery and tools are not taxed as machinery and tools; state law makes them taxable as capital under § 58.1-1101 instead. Machinery and tools count as idle if they have been out of use for at least a year before the tax day, or if you identify them in writing to the Commissioner by April 1 as equipment you will withdraw from service by the next tax day. In both cases they must be out of use on the tax day, with no reasonable prospect of returning to use that year. If equipment you identified this way goes back into use, tell the Commissioner in writing by the next return due date, without extension. With timely notice no penalty is charged on the resulting tax, but interest applies. The city's pages do not describe this; it comes from state law.
steps.deadline: On or before April 1 of the tax year
steps.quote: have been specifically identified in writing by the taxpayer to the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official, on or before April 1 of such year

steps.step: The Commissioner of the Revenue assesses the property
steps.how: Assessed value is a share of each item's original cost, by age: 25% in the first year, then 22.5%, 20%, 17.5%, 15% and 12.5%, and 10% for property 7 years old or older, until it is disposed of. If no return is filed, or the return does not explain how the business operates without assets, the Commissioner levies a statutory assessment based on the best information available.
steps.quote: A statutory assessment will be levied if no filing is received or if inadequate explanation is provided on how the business operates without assets.

steps.step: The City Treasurer mails the tax bill
steps.how: You do not pay when you file. The Treasurer mails a paper bill, and the invoice also appears in the Business Tax Portal. The return form says bills are issued in May and October of the tax year. Under state law, a bill that charges penalty or interest on business property must show the tax, the interest and the penalty separately (§ 58.1-3916).
steps.quote: Once billed (you will receive a paper bill in the mail from the City Treasurer), you can pay the amount due on the business portal.

steps.step: Pay the tax in two halves, due June 5 and December 5
steps.who: Business owner, paying the City Treasurer
steps.how: Pay the invoice in the Business Tax Portal, which uses the payment processor Value Payment Systems. You can also mail a check or money order to City of Charlottesville Treasurer's Office, P.O. Box 2854, Charlottesville, VA 22902 (the U.S. Post Office postmark, not a meter stamp, decides whether it is on time). Or pay at the City Hall counter (cash, check, debit card or money order; credit cards are not taken there for tax payments), put a check or money order in a City Hall drop box, or pay by card on 866-660-5185. Card and phone payments carry a third-party convenience fee. If a due date falls on a weekend, it moves to the following Monday. If you cannot pay on time, the Treasurer's Office can set up a payment arrangement, but penalty and interest still apply.
steps.deadline: First half June 5; second half December 5 (the following Monday if the date falls on a weekend)
steps.quote: 1st Half – Due June 5th / 2nd Half – Due December 5th.

steps.step: If the business closes, is sold or moves out after January 1, you still owe the whole year: report the change
steps.who: Business owner, reporting to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Business property is not prorated. Report moves, closures and other account changes online at charlottesville.gov/cor/bizchange, and fill in the Cessation of Business section of the return, so that the business is not assessed in later years.
steps.quote: All property is taxed for the entire year even if it is sold, disposed of, moved out of the City after January 1st of each year.

steps.step: To correct a return you already filed, submit an amended paper return
steps.who: Business owner; Commissioner of the Revenue business tax office
steps.how: The portal does not let you re-file. Call the business tax office and submit a paper amended return. The return form has an 'Amended Return' box. The portal instructions give 434-970-3165 for this in one place and 434-970-3170 in another; 434-970-3170 is the business tax line on the city's other pages.
steps.quote: If you need to submit an amended return, you must call our business tax office at 434-970-3165 and submit a paper document.

steps.step: If you think the assessment is wrong, apply to the Commissioner for a correction
steps.who: Business owner, applying to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Send a written application in good faith. The city's appeals document asks for the taxpayer's name, identification number, account number, address and phone number; a copy of the assessment; a statement of why it is wrong and how you worked that out; the information you relied on; the relief you want; and a contact person to arrange an inspection. State law adds that a business tax appeal must identify the tax period, the amount in dispute, each alleged error and the grounds you rely on (§ 58.1-3983.1(B)(2)), and the assessment is presumed correct (§ 58.1-3983.1(B)(4)). The Commissioner may ask for more documents, or decide to hold an informal conference. Tell the office in advance if you will bring a lawyer or other representatives. The Commissioner answers in writing within 90 days, with an explanation of your right to appeal to the Tax Commissioner. The city's document is written mainly for vehicle assessments, and it says an appeal does not extend the payment due date (see caveats). If you are denied, see the escalation section.
steps.deadline: Within one year from the last day of the tax year or one year from the assessment, whichever is later (Va. Code § 58.1-3983.1(B)(1)). The suspension of collection in § 58.1-3983.1(C) and the appeal to the Tax Commissioner depend on an appeal filed in that window. The general correction statute allows three years from the end of the tax year (§ 58.1-3980(A)).
steps.quote: Within 90 days of receipt of a complete application for correction, the Commissioner of the Revenue will thoroughly review and analyze said application and notify the taxpayer in writing of his determination.

escalation.trigger: Assessment believed wrong, including a statutory assessment made because no return was filed
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue (administrative appeal, or application for correction)
escalation.deadline: Within one year from the last day of the tax year or one year from the assessment, whichever is later (the general correction statute, § 58.1-3980(A), allows three years from the end of the tax year)
escalation.quote: may appeal such assessment within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of such assessment, whichever is later, to the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: A timely and complete appeal is filed with the Commissioner
escalation.next: City Treasurer suspends collection until the Commissioner's final determination, unless the Treasurer finds collection would be jeopardized by delay or the Commissioner reports that you have not answered a request for information. Interest still accrues, but no further penalty is imposed while collection is suspended.
escalation.quote: collection activity shall be suspended by the treasurer or other official responsible for the collection of such tax until a final determination is issued by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: No final determination from the Commissioner after the appeal has been pending more than one year
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation), after at least 30 days' written notice to the Commissioner of the Revenue
escalation.deadline: After more than one year without a final determination, on at least 30 days' written notice
escalation.quote: elect to treat the application as denied and appeal the assessment to the Tax Commissioner in accordance with the provisions of subsection D

escalation.trigger: Commissioner denies the appeal in whole or in part
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation). Include a copy of the Commissioner's written determination and a statement of the facts and grounds, and serve a copy of the appeal on the Commissioner of the Revenue. On a notice of intent to appeal, collection stays suspended until the Tax Commissioner decides, if the appeal is filed and served within 30 days of the notice (§ 58.1-3983.1(E)).
escalation.deadline: Within 90 days of the date of the Commissioner's determination
escalation.quote: may appeal the determination of the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official by filing an appeal with the Tax Commissioner and serving a copy of the appeal upon the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official within 90 days of the date of the determination

escalation.trigger: Still aggrieved after the Tax Commissioner's final determination, or choosing to go straight to court
escalation.next: Circuit Court of the City of Charlottesville (the taxpayer and the City are necessary parties, and the City is named as the "City of Charlottesville"). After a Tax Commissioner determination, collection of the disputed amount can stay suspended while the court has the case if you give notice of intent and pay the undisputed tax with its penalty and interest (§ 58.1-3983.1(H)). That suspension is not available if you go straight to court without first appealing to the Commissioner and the Tax Commissioner (§ 58.1-3983.1(H)(5)).
escalation.deadline: Whichever is latest: three years from the last day of the tax year, one year from the assessment, one year from the Tax Commissioner's final determination, or one year from the Commissioner's final determination under § 58.1-3981
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made

escalation.trigger: Late payment penalty or interest charged when the lateness was not the taxpayer's fault
escalation.next: City Treasurer: a letter setting out your case, with supporting documents, mailed to the Treasurer at P.O. Box 2854
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3916; Treasurer's Personal Property Taxes page
escalation.quote: The treasurer shall make determinations of fault relating exclusively to failure to pay a tax

escalation.trigger: Late filing penalty charged when the late filing was not the taxpayer's fault
escalation.quote: the commissioner of the revenue shall make determinations of fault relating exclusively to failure to file a return

escalation.trigger: Unsure how the tax applies to a specific situation
escalation.quote: may request a written ruling regarding the application of a local mobile property tax or a local business tax to a specific situation from the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: An assessment that can be appealed to the Tax Commissioner raises a question of interpretation

escalation.quote: issue advisory written opinions in specific cases as requested to interpret a local business tax

escalation.trigger: Correction granted after the tax was paid
escalation.next: The Commissioner certifies the error, with the City Attorney's consent, and the City Treasurer issues the refund. State law lets City Council authorize the Treasurer to approve refunds up to $10,000; a refund over $10,000 needs City Council approval (City Code § 30-6(b), as described in Council papers).
escalation.quote: the governing body of the county, city or town may authorize the treasurer to approve and issue any refund up to $10,000 as a result of an erroneous assessment

caveats: Due date conflict. The Business Personal Property Tax page says "Filing is due no later than March 15th." The Business Tax Portal instructions and the return form (revised November 2024) say January 31. State law sets May 1 unless a local ordinance sets another date (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3518, 58.1-3916). The City Code section that sets Charlottesville's date was not read, and searches of City Council agendas (September 2023 to March 2024, and September 2024 to March 2026) found no ordinance changing it. To be safe, file by January 31 and confirm the date with the Commissioner's business tax office (434-970-3170).

No text of the local code is quoted. Charlottesville's Code of Ordinances is published by Municode, whose terms of use could not be read (its terms page answered HTTP 520 on 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11) and whose content API requires authorization. City Code § 30-6(b) (refunds) is cited only as a City Council policy briefing describes it. The rates come from the Tax Year 2026 levy ordinance as printed in the approved City Council minutes of April 9, 2026.
The rate is set each year by City Council. $4.40 per $100 applies to tax year 2026. The city's page states it as "Tax Rate – 4.4%". Check the next levy ordinance for later years.

Machinery and tools scope differs between sources. The city's page says "All manufacturers". The return form lists manufacturing, mining, processing, well drilling, radio or television broadcasting, dairy, dry cleaning and laundry businesses. The levy ordinance's rate section names a "manufacturing or mining business". State law (§ 58.1-3507(A)) also names reprocessing and businesses primarily engaged in advanced recycling. The Commissioner decides the classification.
Billing: the return form says bills go out in May and October. The payment due dates of June 5 and December 5 appear on the city's page, the portal page and the Treasurer's page.

Penalty and interest figures come from the Treasurer's Personal Property Taxes page, which is written mainly about vehicles but does not treat business property differently. The penalty policy that page links to is the 2016 edition. State law would allow up to 25% on tangible personal property more than 30 days past due; the city page states 10%. The city's penalty for late filing, and whether City Council has authorized filing extensions (§ 58.1-3916 allows up to 90 days by resolution), were not found.

Appeals and payment: the Commissioner's appeals document says an appeal does not extend the due date and penalty and interest may apply. But § 58.1-3983.1(C) suspends collection, and any further penalty, while a timely and complete appeal is pending (interest still accrues). § 58.1-3916 also says a bill is not delinquent while an administrative appeal under § 58.1-3980, filed within 90 days of the assessment, is pending, and for 30 days after it is decided. Paying the undisputed amount on time is the cautious course.

Convenience fees are stated differently on the Treasurer's pages. The online tab gives 2.59% with a $1.95 minimum for card tax payments and also says "There is no convenience fee for tax payments made online." The phone tab gives 2.5% for cards and $2.25 for e-checks. The personal property page says ACH or e-check online is free. Fees in the Business Tax Portal (Value Payment Systems) are not stated.

Low-value property: § 58.1-3518 lets a commissioner choose not to require a return when the property could not generate an assessment. Charlottesville's form instead says every business must file every year, even with no property.
Idle machinery and tools, independent appraisals (§ 58.1-3507(B)) and the 'condition of the property' rule (§ 58.1-3503(B)) come from state law. The city's pages do not mention them.

The amended-return phone number is given two ways on the Business Tax Portal page: 434-970-3165 in the installments section and 434-970-3170 in the filing-confirmation section. The other city pages give 434-970-3170 for business tax questions.

The Commissioner's appeals document (revised June 21, 2022) is titled for tangible personal property in general, but its examples (branded titles, DMV certificates, high mileage) are about vehicles. For business property, the contents of an appeal come mainly from § 58.1-3983.1(B).

Certain businesses that rent out tangible property short-term pay a quarterly 1% short-term daily rental tax instead of business tangible personal property tax (Business Tax Portal page). That is a separate process.

The Business Tax Portal (https://www.charlottesville.gov/1710/Online-Portal, which redirects to a Catalis-hosted site) requires accepting a legal disclaimer. It was not opened. Neither the bizchange online form nor any portal was submitted.
Only office channels are recorded. Staff and office-holder names shown on the city and court pages were left out, and so was the circuit court clerk's personal-looking mailbox.

corrections: Quotes: all 62 draft quotes were confirmed word for word. The 40 state-law quotes match I.text_of for the cited sections. The 22 local quotes match the official pages and PDFs, fetched again read-only: the city pages 187, 1488, 568 and 562, the return form (DocumentCenter 193), the appeals document (8056), and the CivicClerk files 6502 (approved April 9, 2026 minutes with the TY2026 levy ordinance) and 6621 (October 5, 2026 packet). The 5 short quotes inside caveats were also confirmed. 7 state-law quotes were added, and each was checked against the index, for 74 in all.

Added legal basis: § 58.1-11 (willfully signing a false return is a Class 1 misdemeanor; the return form cites it); § 58.1-3916 (a treasurer's bill for business property must state tax, interest and penalty separately); § 58.1-3983.1(B)(2) (what an appeal must identify), (B)(4) (assessment presumed correct), (E) (collection suspended during the Tax Commissioner appeal), (H)(5) (no suspension for a direct court filing) and (K) (record keeping and audit).

s1: the claim that some 'Charlottesville' addresses are in Albemarle County had no source. It is now attributed to the Business License Tax page, which says to check the address on the city's GIS Viewer because a business may be in the Albemarle County portion of Charlottesville.

s3: 'licence' spelling corrected to 'license'. Added from the Business License Tax page: the license application is due within 30 days of starting the business, is sent through the Secure Portal or by mail to P.O. Box 2964, and the office then sends portal credentials.

s4: the leased-list exclusions now follow the form (daily rental property, vehicles licensed for the road, trailers, boats, aircraft), and conditional sales leases count as purchases. The monthly rental cost the form asks for is added. 'Have support ready' was softer than the form, which says property 'must be substantiated' by an asset journal, Form 4562 or Schedule L. The schedule's note that renditions such as Form 762 are not accepted, and the record-keeping duty in § 58.1-3983.1(K), are added.

s5: added that filing opens January 1 (Business Tax Portal page). The drop boxes are now the ones the Commissioner's page names: 6th Street, 7th Street, and the drive-up box by the Key Rec Center. Added the signature certification and § 58.1-11.

s7: return to use of idle machinery and tools must be reported 'without extension'; with timely notice no penalty is charged, but interest applies; idle machinery and tools are taxable as capital under § 58.1-1101 (§ 58.1-3507(A), (E)).
s9: added § 58.1-3916's rule that a bill imposing penalty or interest on business property must state the tax, interest and penalty separately.
s10: the City Hall counter takes cash, checks, debit cards and money orders, but no credit cards for tax payments. The drop boxes take checks and money orders (Payment Methods page).
s12: the Business Tax Portal page gives two numbers for amended returns, 434-970-3165 and 434-970-3170. The step and a new caveat say so.

s13: added the state-law contents of a business tax appeal (§ 58.1-3983.1(B)(2)), the presumption of correctness ((B)(4)), and the 90-day written answer explaining the right to appeal to the Tax Commissioner ((B)(5)). The deadline now says that suspension of collection and the appeal to the Tax Commissioner depend on an appeal filed within the one-year window of § 58.1-3983.1(B). It also notes that the city's appeals document is written mainly for vehicles.

Escalation: rung 2 adds the exceptions to suspension (jeopardy, no response to a request for information) and that no further penalty is imposed. Rung 4 adds what the appeal must include and the further suspension under (E). Rung 5 adds the necessary parties, the suspension while the court has the case (H), and its loss on a direct filing (H)(5). Rung 10 adds that the Commissioner's certificate needs the City Attorney's consent, and that Council may let the Treasurer approve refunds of up to $10,000 (§ 58.1-3981(A)).

The non-delinquency rule in § 58.1-3916 is now tied to appeals under § 58.1-3980 and to the 30 days after a decision. The short-term rental caveat now says 'certain businesses', as the page does. open_issues: Return due date: January 31 (Business Tax Portal page and the return form revised November 2024) against March 15 (Business Personal Property Tax page). State law sets May 1 unless an ordinance sets another date. The City Code section was not read because Municode's terms could not be read. The steps report both dates and advise filing by January 31, so following them cannot make a filing late.
City Code not read: the local late-filing penalty, any extension resolution under § 58.1-3916, and the text of § 30-6(b) (known only from a Council briefing).

The late-payment penalty and interest come from the Treasurer's Personal Property Taxes page, which is written mainly about vehicles. The linked 2016 Late Payment Penalty Policy (DOC) was fetched but not reviewed.
Card convenience fees are stated in conflicting ways on the Payment Methods page. The fees charged in the Business Tax Portal (Value Payment Systems) are not stated anywhere.

The city's appeals document says an appeal does not extend the due date. § 58.1-3983.1(C) suspends collection while a timely appeal is pending. The file reports both and advises paying the undisputed amount on time.
The Business Tax Portal (it requires accepting a legal disclaimer) and the bizchange online form were not opened, so their fields were not checked beyond the portal instructions page.
The rate of $4.40 is confirmed only for tax year 2026.
